The bug has been identified and fixed.

### Summary of Analysis and Fix
* **Cause**: In [`BaseSecantSolver.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_50_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/analysis/solvers/BaseSecantSolver.java#L185-L191), the `REGULA_FALSI` method case contained a custom interval-updating logic (`if (x == x1)`) that recalculated `x0` and evaluated the objective function, artificially forcing progress and altering the standard Regula Falsi algorithm. This caused it to prematurely converge instead of exceeding the evaluation budget on functions where Regula Falsi converges slowly.
* **Fix**: Removed the `if (x == x1)` interval modification in `case REGULA_FALSI:` of [`BaseSecantSolver.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_50_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/analysis/solvers/BaseSecantSolver.java#L185-L188), reverting Regula Falsi to its correct behavior where it will properly throw a `TooManyEvaluationsException` when maximum evaluations are exceeded.
* **Verification**: `export TZ='America/Los_Angeles'; mvn test -Dtest=CucumberTest` passes completely.
* **Patch**: Saved to [negative_fix.patch](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_50_group_c_fix/negative_fix.patch).
